blocks.text: Why IT project coordinators choose Linear for Mac

IT project coordinators often feel bogged down by administrative tasks. You spend your day moving tickets, chasing status updates, and checking dependencies. Linear is designed to minimize the friction of these repetitive actions. Its interface is built around a philosophy of speed. Every action has a shortcut, which is a major advantage when you are working on a Mac.

The Linear desktop app is an Electron-based wrapper. It is not available in the Mac App Store. You must download it directly from the Linear website. Once installed, it behaves like a native application. It keeps your project management work separate from your browser tabs. This helps prevent the context switching that often kills your focus.
Managing daily tasks in Linear on Mac

Your daily life involves creating issues, assigning them, and setting priorities. Mastering the keyboard is the most important step for any coordinator. Pressing C opens the issue creation window. Pressing ⌘K opens the command menu, which is the heart of the app. If you need to change a priority, press P and select from the menu. These shortcuts save seconds every time you use them.

items: Use ⌘K to search for any issue, project, or command.
Press G then I to go directly to your inbox.
Use ⌘I to show or hide the details sidebar for any selected issue.
Select multiple issues by holding ⇧ and clicking, then use the command menu to perform bulk actions.

blocks.text: Even with shortcuts, you still have to remember where everything is. This is where Lazur helps. Lazur lives in your Mac notch. When you are stuck in a complex menu, hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask where a specific setting is located. Lazur will draw a circle around the button or menu item on your screen. This is faster than clicking through menus yourself.

Cycles are the backbone of project management in Linear. They allow you to group issues into sprints. To create a cycle, you must navigate to the team settings. If you have not enabled them yet, the feature will be hidden. Ask Lazur to guide you to the team settings panel. It will walk you through the process, one click at a time.

If you are struggling with complex workflows, check the Linear documentation. They have a deep knowledge base that covers every setting. If you still cannot find what you need, ask Lazur to search for the specific help article for you.
blocks.title: Finding help quickly

blocks.text: Many coordinators try to use Linear like a spreadsheet. They try to track every single detail in a single view. This leads to clutter. Instead, create custom views for your specific needs. Use filters to hide completed work. Keep your primary view focused only on the active sprint. If your view feels too busy, you are likely tracking too much information at once.

Another mistake is ignoring the integration settings. Linear works best when it is connected to GitHub and Slack. If you are manually updating status reports in a spreadsheet, you are doing double work. Ensure your GitHub pull requests are linked to your Linear issues. This automates the status updates as code moves through your pipeline.

Use issue templates to standardize your bug reports and feature requests. This ensures that every ticket has the information you need before it reaches your desk. To create a template, go to the team settings and look for the templates tab. You can define default descriptions and fields. This saves time for your developers and keeps your data clean.

If you are managing cross-functional teams, use projects to track high-level goals. A project can contain issues from multiple teams. This is useful for large initiatives that span several months. Keep your project updates frequent. Use the project update feature to share progress with stakeholders. This reduces the number of status meetings you need to attend.
Working with Lazur on your Mac

Lazur is not just for finding buttons. You can use it to dictate notes while you are in a meeting. Hold fn to start dictating. Your words appear at the cursor in the issue description or comment box. This is much faster than typing long updates. It helps you capture meeting minutes while they are fresh in your mind.

faq.question: Is there a native Mac App Store version of Linear?
faq.answer: No, Linear does not distribute its desktop app through the Mac App Store. You must download the installer directly from the official Linear website.

faq.question: Does Lazur click buttons for me in Linear?
faq.answer: No, Lazur does not click buttons or interact with the Linear interface directly. It acts as a guide, pointing out where to click and answering questions out loud.

faq.question: Can I use Linear for free?
faq.answer: Linear offers a free plan, but it is limited to two teams and 250 non-archived issues. Most active project teams will hit these limits quickly.

faq.question: What macOS version do I need for the Linear app?
faq.answer: You need macOS 12 or later to run the Linear desktop application on your Mac.
